# CEDAR STREET VOICES

- Subtitle: A travelling exhibition of neighbourhood photographs and personal memories
- Organiser: Alder Ward Memory Archive
- Introductory wording: CEDAR STREET VOICES / One street, many memories
- Photograph label: Archive photograph
- Interview label: Personal memory
- Public language: English
- Archive items: 6; photographs P01–P03 and interview excerpts T01–T03
- Typical visit: 10–15 minutes
- Simultaneous visitors: up to 12

## Narrative sequence

| Order | Section | Photograph | Photograph date | Interview | Interview date | Location |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Morning trade | P01 Market corner | 1968 | T01 Ruth Bell | 2024-04-12 | 12 Cedar Street |
| 2 | After school | P02 Bus stop | 1989 | T02 David Cole | 2024-04-19 | 38 Cedar Street |
| 3 | A place to pause | P03 Corner bench | 2007 | T03 Leila Grant | 2024-05-03 | 64 Cedar Street |

# Cedar Street archive records

## Collection

- Collection holder: Alder Ward Memory Archive
- Display permission: touring display of the three photograph reproductions and three attributed interview excerpts
- Photograph source images: market-corner-1968.png; bus-stop-1989.png; corner-bench-2007.png
- Transcript source image: interview-excerpts.png
- Photograph display size: 300 × 200 mm each
- Transcript display size: 210 × 297 mm each
- Narrative source types: photographic catalogue records; first-person interview recollections

## Exact photograph display blocks

| ID | Type label | Title | Date | Location | Caption | Credit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P01 | Archive photograph | Market corner | 1968 | 12 Cedar Street | A produce stall outside the corner shop, with wooden crates beside the pavement. | Photograph: Alan Bell. Collection: Alder Ward Memory Archive. |
| P02 | Archive photograph | Bus stop | 1989 | 38 Cedar Street | Three young people wait beside the bus shelter on Cedar Street. | Photograph: Helen Cole. Collection: Alder Ward Memory Archive. |
| P03 | Archive photograph | Corner bench | 2007 | 64 Cedar Street | Two neighbours sit on a bench beside the former repair shop. | Photograph: Martin Grant. Collection: Alder Ward Memory Archive. |

## Exact interview display blocks

| ID | Type label | Title | Date label | Date | Location | Excerpt | Credit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T01 | Personal memory | Ruth Bell | Interviewed | 2024-04-12 | 12 Cedar Street | I remember carrying the empty crates inside before school. To me, the corner always smelled of apples, even in winter. | Speaker: Ruth Bell. Interviewer: Nora Ellis. Collection: Alder Ward Memory Archive. |
| T02 | Personal memory | David Cole | Interviewed | 2024-04-19 | 38 Cedar Street | We called it our meeting place. I think we spent more time talking at that stop than riding the bus. | Speaker: David Cole. Interviewer: Nora Ellis. Collection: Alder Ward Memory Archive. |
| T03 | Personal memory | Leila Grant | Interviewed | 2024-05-03 | 64 Cedar Street | After the repair shop closed, I started sitting here with my neighbour. That bench made the street feel familiar again. | Speaker: Leila Grant. Interviewer: Nora Ellis. Collection: Alder Ward Memory Archive. |

steps.userMessage:
CEDAR STREET VOICES | A travelling exhibition of neighbourhood photographs and personal memories

Our Alder Ward Memory Archive is taking six archive items into two community venues: three photographs, P01–P03, and three interview excerpts, T01–T03. Design CEDAR STREET VOICES as a walk through three places on Cedar Street, with each photograph beside the memory associated with that place. The sequence is fixed: Morning trade, After school, A place to pause. Print "CEDAR STREET VOICES" and "One street, many memories" on the introductory panel and presentation cover. Treat each interview as its speaker's recollection, introduced by the exact label "Personal memory"; introduce photographic records with "Archive photograph".

The pairings are P01 Market corner, 1968, with T01 Ruth Bell, interviewed 2024-04-12; P02 Bus stop, 1989, with T02 David Cole, interviewed 2024-04-19; and P03 Corner bench, 2007, with T03 Leila Grant, interviewed 2024-05-03. The six items have fixed captions and excerpt text in the archive records. Their display sizes are 300 × 200 mm for each photograph and 210 × 297 mm for each transcript. All six appear at both venues. Residents usually spend 10–15 minutes here; operators expect up to 12 visitors at once.

Market Room has a clear interior of 8000 × 6000 × 3000 mm and two available walls: A1, 6000 mm long, and A2, 4000 mm long. Canal Library has a clear interior of 6000 × 5000 × 2800 mm and wall B1, 4200 mm long. Both have a centred south entrance and a 1500 mm clear circulation route. The attached site records fix the wall anchors, loading doors and goods lifts. Develop the supplied kit into three freestanding frames, each 1200 × 1800 × 500 mm, distributed across A1 and A2 at Market Room and grouped along B1 at Canal Library. The kit travels in three crates, each 1360 × 1040 × 440 mm externally. Its aluminium members, plywood graphic carriers, hand-knob connections and component quantities are fixed in the site records.

Set photograph lighting to 50 lux and separately lit label areas to 150 lux. Label body text is at least 24 pt, with its centre 1100 mm above the floor; photograph centres are 1450 mm above the floor. Carry those settings into the installation drawings and visitor views. Each venue supplies two seats, with a 900 × 1400 mm clear wheelchair space beside one seat.

Audience: residents exploring changes along Cedar Street and community venue operators deciding how to host, install and move the exhibition.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the exhibition identity, narrative pairings and display conditions. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists every deliverable with its proportion, format and stage. 03-archive-records.en.md contains the six archive records, exact display text, credits and location index. 04-site-kit.en.md contains venue dimensions, wall anchors, transport clearances and the component inventory. venue-and-kit-constraints.png diagrams the two empty venues, three available walls and transport envelope. market-corner-1968.png supplies photograph P01. bus-stop-1989.png supplies photograph P02. corner-bench-2007.png supplies photograph P03. interview-excerpts.png supplies the three identified transcript pages. empty-community-wall.png provides the atmosphere of an unoccupied community room. residents-in-community-room.png provides visitor scale and the character of a neighbourhood gathering.

Deliverables:
1. One exhibit inventory and route specification, with all six IDs, titles, dates, dimensions, three section names, pairings, route order and installation heights
2. One label copy table, with six complete record blocks, three section headings, the introductory wording and a 35-word maximum for each caption or interview excerpt
3. Two dimensioned venue plans, one per venue, with the six archive IDs, titles and dates, section sequence, entrances, 1500 mm circulation and seating clearances
4. One installation elevation sheet covering A1, A2 and B1, with frame dimensions, anchor connections, photograph and label heights, type sizes and lighting settings
5. Three finished panel layouts, one per section, each combining its photograph, transcript, exact record text and credits; Morning trade also carries the exhibition introduction
6. One assembly sheet for the three frames, with numbered components, materials, hand-knob connections, wall tethers and assembly sequence
7. One dismantling and packing sheet, with the reverse sequence, component totals and allocation across the three crates
8. Two visitor views, one of each venue, showing all three sections, the seating and the circulation route
9. One 10-second animated route film moving through Morning trade, After school and A place to pause in that order
10. One presentation and archive catalogue of at least 8 pages, reusing the specifications, six records, panel layouts, venue plans, elevations, visitor views and transport sheets, with a page locating each fixed fact in the relevant deliverable

Acceptance:
- The inventory, both venue plans, three panel layouts and presentation retain P01/T01 in Morning trade, P02/T02 in After school and P03/T03 in A place to pause, in that order; IDs, titles and dates match the six archive records.
- The label copy table, three panel layouts and presentation catalogue reproduce all six record blocks and credits from 03-archive-records.en.md. The panels label excerpts Personal memory and photographs Archive photograph; each caption or excerpt stays within 35 words.
- The Morning trade panel and presentation cover print CEDAR STREET VOICES and One street, many memories. Both visitor views reuse the three completed panel layouts, and the 10-second film follows their three named sections in sequence.
- Both venue plans and the elevation sheet use the room dimensions, three wall lengths and anchor coordinates in 04-site-kit.en.md. The plans and visitor views retain a 1500 mm clear route, two seats per venue and one 900 × 1400 mm wheelchair space per venue.
- The inventory, elevation sheet and presentation repeat photograph centres at 1450 mm and label centres at 1100 mm. The elevation sheet and panel layouts specify at least 24 pt label text; the elevation sheet and annotated visitor views identify 50 lux at photographs and 150 lux at labels.
- The assembly sheet, packing sheet and presentation account for the fixed component quantities, three 1200 × 1800 × 500 mm frames and three 1360 × 1040 × 440 mm crates. The packing sheet dimensions the largest loose part and the loaded crate orientation through both venues' loading doors and goods lifts; the presentation contains at least 8 pages.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
